name: granulator3
description:
Granulator 3  --  generated by scripts/gen/gen_granulator3.py; edit the generator.

A dense, textural granular cloud: up to 64 overlapping grains read from one
source, each with its own envelope shape and its own place in a multichannel
speaker ring.

Scheduling
----------
`density` is the number of voices running at once.  A voice plays one grain,
waits a random gap set by `jitter`, then starts the next grain.  Each grain
latches all of its parameters when it starts and holds them for its whole
life, so moving a control only affects later grains and never tears one that
is sounding.  That also means the grain controls need no smoothing.

Random draws come from a stateless hash of (grain count, voice index), so a
render is deterministic.  A voice's next grain is prepared once per block,
outside crag.per_sample, which keeps the per-sample loop down to a sampler
read and the envelope.  A voice that finishes two grains inside one block
repeats the same parameters for the second.

Envelopes
---------
`shape` morphs continuously through six stops, and `shape_spread` gives each
grain its own random offset from it, so one cloud can mix shapes:

  0 expodec    instant attack, long decay
  1 gaussian   narrow bell
  2 hann       the default; smooth overlap
  3 sine       equal-power overlap, the densest and flattest wash
  4 tukey      flat top with short tapered edges
  5 rexpodec   long swell, instant release

Every stop is one formula with different coefficients:

  t   = min(phase / skew, (1 - phase) / (1 - skew))     skewed triangle
  s   = sin(pi/2 * min(t / taper, 1))
  env = w1*s + w2*s^2 + w4*s^4

so morphing costs no extra evaluations and needs no libm call per sample.
Grain gain is normalised by each stop's 1/rms, which keeps the shapes at a
similar loudness.

Multichannel spread
-------------------
The output is a 7.1 speaker field (FL FR FC LFE BL BR SL SR).  A grain sits
at a point on the speaker ring and pans equal-power between the two nearest
speakers by angle:

  FC 0   FR 30   SR 90   BR 150   BL 210   SL 270   FL 330   degrees, clockwise

  position = center + orbit * time + spread * (random - 0.5)   in revolutions

spread = 0 stacks every grain at `center`; spread = 1 scatters them around
the whole ring; `orbit` rotates the whole cloud, including sounding grains.
The LFE stays silent.  The engine's layout-aware mixers fold the field to
the host's width (stereo, quad, 5.1 or mono) by speaker position, so the
graph needs no layout setting.  The field is scaled by sqrt(7/2), so that
after an equal-power fold each host channel is about as loud as one channel
of a stereo granulator.  Pan gains move on a per-block linear ramp, so a new
grain's position glides in over at most one block rather than clicking.

Controls
--------
  density       [1, 64]     simultaneous voices; fractional values fade the top voice
  grain_ms      [5, 2000]   centre grain length
  grain_var     [0, 1]      random length range, up to +/-2 octaves
  jitter        [0, 1]      random gap after each grain, up to 2x its length
  position      [0, 1]      source read position
  scatter       [0, 1]      random read offset as a fraction of the file
  scan          [-2, 2]     moves position through the file; 1 = source speed
  pitch         [-24, 24]   semitones
  pitch_spread  [0, 24]     random per-grain detune, +/- semitones
  reverse       [0, 1]      probability a grain plays backwards
  shape         [0, 5]      envelope morph (see above)
  shape_spread  [0, 1]      random per-grain shape offset
  spread        [0, 1]      how far grains scatter around the ring
  center        [0, 1]      ring position of the cloud; 0 = front
  orbit         [-2, 2]     cloud rotation in revolutions per second
  output_gain   [0, 2]      output level, followed by a soft limiter above 0.8

Sampler:  "audio" - bind a WAV via crag_bind_audio_by_index(0, ptr, len).
Output:   !crag.audio<f32, 48000, 8> (7.1), folded by the engine to the host width.

Visualizer: "granulator3_viz" - source + live grains, envelopes, speaker ring.
